ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: "different kinds." In Chan questions it can stand alone: asked "what are the other kinds?" (如何是異類), the identified master strikes a bowl and calls a servant to eat, while another answers "the foot is short, the inch is long" (尺短寸長).
EvidenceBody: Its defining Zen deployment is the fixed expression "move among other kinds" (異類中行). Nanquan says people of the time must move among other kinds; challenged on "kind," he puts both hands on the ground. Another witness places the expression beside "although moving in an animal's conduct, one does not receive an animal's recompense" (雖行畜生行，不得畜生報). Cao Dong's record supplies the sharpest lexical boundary: the ancients provisionally borrowed the water buffalo as an "other kind"; it is an other kind in the matter, not an other kind in language (古人權借水牯牛為異類。秖是事上異類。非言語中異類). The entry records these answers and boundaries without deciding what spiritual condition they express.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: The stored cases establish the corpus-specific deployment of 異類 stated in the opening.
